title: Knowledge transfer between simple discrete worlds
abstract: arXiv:2610.15081v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adapting to a new world and reasoning correctly about which outcomes are possible under rules one has not met before is a basic capacity underlying general intelligence. We study it in small discrete worlds: sets of grid configurations consistent with a shared set of rules, concretely Sudoku-like puzzles built from a common base and a handful of extra rules. We train a single depth-recurrent model on many combinations of rules and test it at four levels of novelty: a new puzzle, a new combination of known rules, a pairing of rules never seen together, and a rule instance not seen at all during training. The model receives the active rules either as a symbolic description or as two solved examples, and a model that gets no rule information is used as a baseline. translated_title: 简单离散世界之间的知识迁移
translated_abstract: 适应新世界并在未曾遇到过的规则下正确推理哪些结果是可能的，是支撑通用智能的一项基本能力。我们在小型离散世界中研究这一能力：即与一组共享规则相一致的网格配置集合，具体为由共同基础加少量额外规则构建的类数独谜题。我们在许多规则组合上训练单个深度循环模型，并在四个新颖性层次上进行测试：新谜题、已知规则的新组合、从未同时出现过的规则配对，以及训练期间完全未见过的规则实例。模型以符号描述或两个已解示例的形式接收当前生效的规则，并以不接收任何规则信息的模型作为基线。在重新组合其训练过的规则时，符号描述方式的效果与示例方式相当或更优（在新组合上分别为99%对95%）。对于其组成部分从未共同出现过的规则实例……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文在类数独离散谜题上研究知识迁移，通过以符号描述或解题示例方式向单个深度循环模型提供规则，发现符号描述在重组已知规则时达到99%的准确率、优于示例方式（95%），并展示了模型在多个新颖性层次上对未见规则进行推理的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper studies knowledge transfer in Sudoku-like discrete worlds by feeding a single depth-recurrent model rules as either symbolic descriptions or solved examples, showing that symbolic descriptions match or exceed examples when recombining trained rules (99% vs. 95%) across four levels of novelty.
